what_its_for: Fosphenytoin is used to treat and prevent seizures, including severe seizures called status epilepticus. It works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain that cause seizures. It is also used before or after brain surgery to help prevent seizures.
how_to_take: This medicine is given by a nurse or doctor as an injection into a vein (IV) or into a muscle (IM) in a hospital or clinic setting. You will not give this medication to yourself at home. Your healthcare team will carefully control how fast the medicine goes into your body. Always stay at the hospital or clinic during and after your treatment so the staff can watch for any side effects.
dosing: The dose of fosphenytoin is carefully calculated by your doctor based on your weight, the type of seizure being treated, and how your body responds to the medicine. Doses are measured in PE units (phenytoin equivalents). Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Never try to adjust the dose on your own. Common doses range from 10 to 20 PE units per kilogram of body weight for emergency seizures, but your medical team will determine what is right for you.
missed_dose: Because fosphenytoin is given in a hospital or clinic by a healthcare professional, you are unlikely to miss a dose. If you have concerns about your treatment schedule, talk to your doctor or nurse right away. Do not try to give yourself this medicine at home.
storage: Fosphenytoin is stored and handled by hospital or pharmacy staff. It is kept in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). It should not be frozen. The prepared solution can be kept at room temperature for up to 24 hours. You do not need to worry about storing this medicine yourself.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while being treated with fosphenytoin, as it can increase side effects and affect seizure control. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do any activity that requires alertness until you know how this medicine affects you, since it can cause dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid suddenly stopping any seizure medicines without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take because fosphenytoin can interact with many medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency help right away if you experience: a severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling skin (these could be signs of a serious reaction called Stevens-Johnson syndrome); swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; trouble breathing; irregular heartbeat or your heart beating very fast or very slow; severe dizziness or fainting; confusion or unusual behavior changes; yellowing of your skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); numbness or tingling at the injection site; pain, redness, or swelling where the shot was given; or any new or worsening side effects. Also tell your doctor if you feel depressed, have thoughts of self-harm, or notice mood changes.
when_it_works: Fosphenytoin starts working quickly because it is given directly into the bloodstream. It converts to phenytoin in your body within about 15 minutes after an IV injection. You may notice seizure activity slowing down or stopping within minutes to hours of receiving the medicine. Your doctor will monitor your response to make sure the medicine is working properly.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Fosphenytoin can harm an unborn baby and may cause birth defects. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. This medicine may also make birth control pills less effective. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Fosphenytoin can be used in children and newborns, but the dose will be carefully adjusted for their weight and age. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness and low blood pressure and will be monitored closely. Kidney or liver problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, your doctor will adjust your dose because the medicine is processed differently in your body.
